title.en: Spot the joke behind the words
title.es: Detectar la broma tras las palabras

es: Reconocer cuándo una frase dice lo contrario de lo que significa (ironía) o resta importancia a un problema grande (understatement).

vocabulary.es: literal, al pie de la letra
atenuación (decir menos de lo que pasa)
en broma, sin hablar en serio

teaching.en: When Tom, soaked to the skin, says “Lovely weather”, his remark is ironic, because the words contradict the situation.
teaching.es: Cuando Tom, empapado hasta los huesos, dice «Qué tiempo tan agradable», su comentario es irónico, porque las palabras contradicen la situación.
teaching.explanationEs: Ironía: dice lo contrario de lo que piensa; el contexto (empapado) delata la intención.
segments: When Tom, soaked to the skin, says “Lovely weather”, his
remark is ironic, because the words contradict the situation.
teaching.audioText: When Tom, soaked to the skin, says “Lovely weather”, his remark is ironic, because the words contradict the situation.

teaching.en: Speakers who play down bad news use understatement: a flooded kitchen becomes “a bit of a disaster”.
teaching.es: Quienes quitan importancia a las malas noticias usan la atenuación: una cocina inundada se convierte en «un pequeño desastre».
teaching.explanationEs: Understatement: se dice menos de lo que ocurre; «a bit of a…» es su fórmula más típica.
segments: Speakers who play down bad news use understatement: a
flooded kitchen becomes “a bit of a disaster”.
teaching.audioText: Speakers who play down bad news use understatement: a flooded kitchen becomes “a bit of a disaster”.

teaching.en: Not everything should be taken at face value: “The soup is hot” is literal when steam is rising from the bowl.
teaching.es: No todo debe tomarse tal cual: «La sopa está caliente» es literal cuando sube vapor del plato.
teaching.explanationEs: Literal: las palabras y la situación coinciden, así que no hay nada oculto.
segments: Not everything should be taken at face value: “The soup is
hot” is literal when steam is rising from the bowl.
teaching.audioText: Not everything should be taken at face value: “The soup is hot” is literal when steam is rising from the bowl.

teaching.en: What speakers mean is often hidden in a dry tone: “That was not exactly a holiday” can describe six hours of rain.
teaching.es: Lo que quieren decir los hablantes suele esconderse en un tono seco: «Eso no fueron precisamente unas vacaciones» puede describir seis horas de lluvia.
teaching.explanationEs: «Not exactly» suaviza un juicio muy negativo; el tono seco lo delata.
segments: What speakers mean is often hidden in a dry tone: “That
was not exactly a holiday” can describe six hours of rain.
teaching.audioText: What speakers mean is often hidden in a dry tone: “That was not exactly a holiday” can describe six hours of rain.

teaching.en: To read between the lines, ask whether the words fit the facts; if the failure is painfully obvious, praise is ironic.
teaching.es: Para leer entre líneas, pregúntate si las palabras encajan con los hechos; si el fracaso es dolorosamente evidente, el elogio es irónico.
teaching.explanationEs: Método: compara lo dicho con lo ocurrido antes de decidir la intención.
segments: To read between the lines, ask whether the words fit the
facts; if the failure is painfully obvious, praise is ironic.
teaching.audioText: To read between the lines, ask whether the words fit the facts; if the failure is painfully obvious, praise is ironic.

teaching.en: Friends who speak tongue in cheek often keep a straight face, so only the situation shows that they do not mean it.
teaching.es: Los amigos que hablan en broma suelen mantener la cara seria, así que solo la situación muestra que no lo dicen en serio.
teaching.explanationEs: Tongue in cheek: dicho sin seriedad, con una cara que no revela la broma.

prompt.es: Mia repara la cadena de la bici: ¿qué quiere decir en realidad con su frase?

choices.text: She enjoyed the repair more than she expected.
She thinks the job was a simple one.
She is annoyed that Leo caused the damage.

feedback.es: El elogio choca con dos horas de trabajo y manos negras de aceite: es ironía y esconde su fastidio con Leo.

hint.es: Compara el elogio con lo que le ha costado a Mia la tarde.

origin.text: Mia has just spent two hours repairing the chain that Leo broke, and her hands are black with oil. She looks at them slowly and says, “Well, that was a great use of my afternoon.”

feedback.es: Play down significa quitar importancia a algo grave; es lo que hace la directora con «a slight inconvenience».

hint.es: Verbo frasal: «jugar» + una dirección hacia abajo.

origin.text: The whole office was flooded on Monday, and the manager wanted to reassure everyone. She tried to ___ the problem by calling it “a slight inconvenience”.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con la idea que transmite.

pairs.es: voz seca que no revela la broma
captar lo que no se dice

feedback.es: Las cuatro expresiones describen cómo se dice o cómo se interpreta un comentario, más allá de las palabras literales.

hint.es: Piensa en quién habla y en quién interpreta.

pairs.es: voz seca que no revela la broma
captar lo que no se dice

prompt.es: Escucha la anécdota: ¿qué hace el hermano con su respuesta a la recepcionista?

choices.text: He plays down a series of serious problems.
He describes the journey exactly as it happened.
He complains loudly about the airline and the hotel.

feedback.es: Retraso, maleta perdida y habitación cedida son problemas serios; llamarlos «a mixed start» es un understatement.

origin.audio: Our flight was delayed for nine hours, the airline lost my suitcase, and the hotel had given our room to somebody else. When the receptionist asked my brother how the journey had been, he said, with a perfectly straight face, that it had been “a bit of a mixed start”.

prompt.es: Lee el correo: ¿qué actitud deja ver quien lo escribe?

choices.text: Sincere thanks, since the delay allowed a useful chat.
Quiet anger hidden behind exaggerated praise.
Calm acceptance of a delay the writer had expected.
Regret at having ignored the warning.

feedback.es: «Only three hours» y «a great success» suenan a elogio, pero describen un atasco: la queja se esconde tras un agradecimiento exagerado.

origin.text: Thank you for warning us about the traffic. We only spent three hours in the queue, and I am sure the extra time in the car was good for our conversation. The children are still speaking to us, so I suppose the day was a great success.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Nadie tomó sus elogios al pie de la letra.»

answer.text: Nobody took his praise at face value

feedback.es: Take + algo + at face value es la estructura fija para aceptar lo dicho sin cuestionarlo.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato: ¿qué da a entender la vecina con su comentario sobre el viaje?

choices.text: That she regrets having planned a journey for that week.
That the snow has been only a minor nuisance for the village.
That the situation is serious, but she prefers to treat it lightly.
That she is annoyed with the reporter for arriving so late.

feedback.es: Nueve días aislados hacen de «not exactly the best week» un understatement: la vecina quita importancia a algo grave con humor.

origin.audio: Last winter my village was cut off by snow for nine days. The power failed, the only shop ran out of bread, and the road disappeared under a metre of white. On the third day a reporter arrived on foot and asked my neighbour how everyone was feeling. She sighed, looked at the drifts and said that it had not exactly been the best week for travelling. The reporter wrote it down as if it were a serious remark. The rest of us laughed for an hour, because my neighbour had not left her kitchen since Sunday and had baked forty loaves to feed the street.

prompt.es: ¿Qué pretende quien escribe este correo a su empleado?

choices.text: To thank the writer for protecting the client's feelings.
To ask the writer politely for a shorter version of the report.
To warn the board that the client was upset by the figures.
To complain about the omissions while seeming to praise them.

feedback.es: Elogia justo lo que no debería haberse hecho (omitir cifras) y cierra con «transparency»: la crítica va envuelta en un elogio irónico.

origin.text: Thanks for your report. I read it on the train and was surprised by how brave you were to leave out every figure that might have upset the client. It is, of course, the kind of omission that makes my job very simple. I shall be sure to tell the board how well you understand our commitment to transparency.

prompt.es: Completa: «Su tono me obligó a leer entre líneas.»

feedback.es: Read between the lines es la expresión fija para captar lo que el texto no dice abiertamente; aquí, el enojo de la tía.

origin.text: My aunt wrote that the party had been “a perfect success” and that nobody had “noticed” the burnt cake. She never says what she really thinks, so I had to read between the ___ to understand that she was upset.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada comentario con el tipo que es en su situación.

pairs: “Brilliant service,” said after waiting two hours for a coffee

pairs.es: irónico: dice lo contrario de lo que piensa

pairs: “Brilliant service,” said when the coffee arrives at once

pairs.es: literal: lo dicho coincide con los hechos

pairs: “It is a bit cold,” said while standing in a storm at midnight
“Not my finest hour,” said after dropping the wedding cake

feedback.es: Cada frase se clasifica comparando lo dicho con la situación: contradicción, coincidencia o minimización.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la postura del autor del blog sobre el humor británico?

choices.text: It is indirect rather than unfriendly, and must be interpreted.
It is cold, but visitors are too quick to take offence.
It is best avoided by anyone who cannot read faces.
It is always ironic, so compliments are never sincere.

feedback.es: El autor rechaza que sea «cold»: lo llama «careful» y propone comprobar cada elogio contra los hechos, no descartarlos todos.

origin.text: People tell me that British humour is cold. I would say it is merely careful: we rarely announce our feelings, so a polite “that was interesting” after a terrible dinner can mean almost anything. The key is to watch the face, weigh the situation and never take a compliment at face value until you have checked it against the facts.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Lo dijo en broma, así que nadie se ofendió.»

answer.text: He said it tongue in cheek, so nobody was offended

feedback.es: Tongue in cheek se coloca tras el verbo y avisa de que no hay intención seria.

prompt.es: Escucha el final del partido: ¿qué pretende el entrenador con su comentario?

choices.text: To praise the creativity of the players sincerely.
To say that the defeat was just bad luck.
To blame the team without saying so directly.

feedback.es: Nueve goles en contra y un tono seco convierten «a great deal of creativity» en una crítica velada, no en un elogio.

origin.audio: After the final whistle, our coach, who had just watched us lose by nine goals, folded his arms and remarked in a dry tone that we had certainly shown a great deal of creativity.
